Notes

Public attention becomes heat, the body becomes a snowman, and a morning phone call asks the vanished person to choose a new self.

下场会很惨

下场 is an outcome with a punitive shade: what becomes of somebody after an action. The opening connects it to not following another person’s instructions, then says the lesson has already been experienced. Before the ambition and self-confidence arrive, the song establishes a voice that remembers disobedience as something with a price.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
苦味回荡悠长

Taste is described through duration and sound: bitterness reverberates. 苦 can already mean suffering as well as bitter flavor, so the line makes an unpleasant experience remain sensory after it is over. Its return before the new verse prevents the later efforts toward perfection from sounding untouched by what happened earlier.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
横冲直撞

横冲直撞 means barging about heedlessly, charging across and colliding. It rubs against the next ambition to be flawless: the method is rough while the desired result is immaculate. That friction makes the speaker’s self-description less straightforwardly heroic. Constant movement may express determination, but it is not evidence that the route is under control.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
浑身解数

解数, pronounced xièshù in this expression, is a repertoire of moves or techniques; 浑身解数 puts the whole body’s resources into use. “Every trick” here is every available skill, not necessarily deception. The phrase adds bodily effort to the claim of trying different angles, just before that same body becomes unable to withstand attention.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
目中无人

目中无人 literally places nobody else in one’s eyes: treating other people as beneath notice. A few lines later everyone’s gaze and the camera are fixed on him. That reversal changes who controls looking. The posture of ignoring others does not stop being exposed to them, and the bright attention soon becomes physically destructive.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
很宁静很孤独

宁静 and 孤独 share the same doubled 很 structure: very quiet, very alone. The next line abruptly adds being watched by everyone. Solitude and exposure therefore coexist rather than alternate. The song separates having attention from having company, which prepares the unreachable relief of the ice bucket.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
打的光很亮

打光 is setting or throwing light for a camera, a practical term from image-making. The next line turns that artificial light into sunlight heating the body. The shift is the hinge of the transformation: a professional condition of being seen becomes an elemental force, making the later snowman image feel earned by the sequence.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
冰桶就在眼前我却够不到

Relief is not distant or invisible; it is right in front of him. 够不到 specifically makes it beyond the reach of the body. That is a sharper frustration than simply being overheated: the scene supplies a recognizable solution while withholding the ability to use it. The subsequent discovery that he is a snowman makes the urgency retroactive.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
雪人

The revelation is delayed: only after camera lights, heat and unreachable ice does he discover he is a snowman. Earlier details suddenly become parts of the same threat. Being illuminated, normally a sign of recognition, is precisely what this body cannot survive. The verse makes visibility and disappearance consequences of the same process, rather than opposite outcomes.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
感受不到身体的重量

Losing weight could have sounded like release from the tape’s many burdens, but here it marks physical disappearance. The snowman does not become freer; he loses the form by which he could be recognized. The line turns lightness into another danger, complicating the usual contrast between oppressive weight and welcome relief.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
历史长河

历史长河 is the familiar “long river of history,” an expansive image for time and collective memory. His melted body enters it as an unrecognizable puddle. The grand scale does not preserve him; it dissolves his identity further. The next line states the fear plainly: the name and person may be lost even if some material trace remains.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
懵逼

懵逼 is coarse, colloquial language for being completely stunned or confused. It breaks the elevated “river of history” register with an everyday, profane morning. “What the fuck” keeps that rupture in English. The phone then rings as if an ordinary day can resume, though the preceding scene has just made an ordinary, stable self difficult to take for granted.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
今天想变成谁

The final question is who he wants to become today, not what he wants to do. After the cameras and melting body, an everyday phone call treats identity as the item that needs choosing. It brings the surreal sequence back into a practical routine while leaving its central problem intact: being expected to appear before others as someone definite.

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
